To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD28/CD4BB costimulatory CARs activate similar signaling pathways, but that the magnitude of signal strength correlates with T cell phenotype and function.

1) CARs containing the CD28 costimulatory domain activate stronger and faster signaling than do CARs containing the 4 1bb costimulatory domain; 2) the strength of CAR T cell signaling is related to the association of Lck and the CAR CD28 costimulatroy domain; and 3) the strength of T cell signaling is an important determinant of T cell function and fate.

CARs with different signaling domains activate similar signaling intermediates, but the strength of signaling is a key determinant in T cell fate and function and that CAR signal strength is partly determined by the affinity of signaling domain interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of signaling pathways and the development of CAR T cells.
the design of a new generation of CARs that are able to induce T cells to kill cancer cells.
the development of new methods for the treatment of cancer and autoimmune diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAR costimulation domains do not predict the signaling pathway activated in CAR T cell but that the strength of CAR signal is a key determinant for T cell fate.
CARs with CD3 and 4-1BB signaling domains activate similar signaling cascades in primary human CD28/CD8+ T cells.
the strength of the CAR T cell signal is a key determinant in T cell fate, and that signal strength can be manipulated to optimize CAR design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strength of signaling is a key determinant for T cell fate.
CD28 and 4  1BB costimulation are not equivalent and that the signaling intensity of a CAR construct is a key factor determining the fate of CAR T cells.
CAR T cell function is dictated by the signaling strength and not by the signaling pathways activated, and that CAR T cell potency can be optimized through tuning of signaling strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CAR signal strength is a major determinant of T cell phenotype and function.
the strength of the signaling initiated by the CAR is an important factor in determining the phenotype and function of CAR T cells.
the strength of CAR signaling can influence the fate of CAR T cells, which may explain the observed differences in clinical efficacy and toxicity of CAR T cells with different signaling domains.
